messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Phantom Variables
parts:
Yves,

I just came back to a script that I worked on last year (using a version of lavaan in the 0.4-* family), and it no longer works.  I use 2 latent variables to define 2 phantom variables in order to estimate the factor covariance as a factor correlation.  This is useful when comparing factor correlations across groups, but when the factor variances are not equal across groups (so the factor covariances would be in different metrics).  I do this by fixing the lower-order factor variances to zero, freely estimate the beta paths from the phantom to the constructs (which represent the standard deviation of the factors), and fix the higher-order (i.e., phantom) factor variances to 1.  This is depicted in the attached path diagram.

When I create the syntax object and run lavaanify(), the parameter table shows that the lower-order factor variances are fixed (free == 0) to zero (start == 0), and the higher-order factor variances are fixed to 1, as the syntax specifies.  Likewise, when I run the model in lavaan(), the parameter table slot matches the lavaanify() object.  However, the results show that the lower-order factor variances are being fixed to 1 instead of 0 (see parameters in rows 9 and 10 of parameter table).

I have also attached the data file and the R syntax.  I would guess that this is a bug, simply because the parameters are being fixed to different values than what the parameter table says.  But since they have to do with phantom variables, I wonder whether there is simply some default that is not being overridden by the syntax.

Thanks for your help,

Terry Jorgensen
